reason: Check all implementation decisions against repository evidence, including token safety, target-service ownership, Caddy, UI, migration, and the executable matrix.
Validate the change preserves parent target architecture, MCP scope, authorization, and coexistence constraints.
Review OAuth/MCP discovery, PKCE, resource binding, errors, refresh, principal, and official-client interoperability behavior.
Check digest handling, recent auth, audit, session/state lifecycle, public/private routing, and required security tests.
Check every tool delegates to current target authorization, preserves dependent ACL actions/non-disclosure, and never allows target fallback.
Check MCP file upload/download operations retain target authorization, versioning, bounded transfer, and secret-safe storage behavior.
Check search/Ask source privacy, revocation races, cancellation, citations, and absence of legacy/public fallback.
Check migrations stay in ima and have fresh/repeat PostgreSQL evidence.
Check OAuth and Problem Details errors expose no secret, internal detail, or protected content.
Check audit/log/metric redaction for codes, tokens, secrets, authorization headers, and content.
Run and review required backend lint, type, pytest, import-safety, and duplication constraints.
Check consent/service UI uses generated DTOs, cookie/CSRF transport, safe state handling, and no credential persistence.
Check workspace-admin UI capability controls, conflicts, access revocation, and server denial coverage.
Check operation IDs, generated API drift, handwritten client location, type safety, and Caddy route coverage.
Check client-side upload/download flows remain target-backed and do not persist protected material.
Check browser search/Ask data privacy, cancellation, and no fallback behavior where MCP administration surfaces it.
